text:
alex: :rotating_light: Getting multiple customer reports that on-call didn't receive pages for the alert window starting ~10:03 UTC. Pagerbot shows pages as sent but no ack events from oncall.
maya: I see alert spikes around 10:02-10:05. Our notify service logs show HTTP 429s from primary-sms-gw during that window.
ops-bot: [automated] alert-forwarder: queued 63 pagers -> attempted fanout to sms-primary and sms-fallback.
rebecca: Paging suppression flags look off — suppressor returned true for several routes. Anyone touched the ratecap config overnight?
jon: I rolled a small change to the notify suppressor config in canary at 02:30 to add a graceful backoff, but it shouldn't flip suppressor=true unless gateway returns 429 repeatedly.
alex: ok let's triage live. Priority: ensure pages go out. Plan: (1) switch traffic to fallback sms provider, (2) disable suppressor for prod for 15m, (3) manual pagers for oncall while we validate.
maya: switching routing now: `k8s exec -n infra notify-router -- set-route sms=secondary --dry-run=false` — doing it.
ops-bot: [automated] notify-router: route update applied, sms -> sms-fallback, started draining sms-primary.
sms-gw-bot: [automated] sms-fallback: health ok. queued messages: 58.
rebecca: disabling suppressor for the paging route: `curl -XPOST https://ops-internal/configs/suppressor/prod/paging -d '{"enabled":false}'` — applied.
alex: manual calls to oncall started; rebecca heading the calls. @rebecca update when first ack received.
rebecca: got first live ack from oncall at 10:10 via phone. still seeing some missed auto-acks.
jon: pulled logs from primary gateway: sample:
```
2026-03-17T10:02:47Z notify -> sms-primary POST /send 429 {"retry_after":30}
2026-03-17T10:02:48Z notify -> sms-primary POST /send 429 {"retry_after":30}
2026-03-17T10:03:01Z suppressor: route=paging evaluated=true reason=rate-window-exceeded
```
maya: looks like primary hit quota and responded with 429s; our suppressor saw the window and suppressed further sends. fallback should be handling now.
alex: good. keep suppressor off for 20m to catch late alerts. Jon, can you open a short-lived runbook to force fanout to both providers until we have a safe config?
jon: creating runbook and a temporary triage tag. `runbook create "sms-fanout-temp" --ttl=30m --actions "fanout-both, disable-suppressor-prod"`
ops-bot: [automated] runbook created: sms-fanout-temp by jon (ttl 30m)
rebecca: posting a customer-facing note to status page: "Paging delivery intermittent between 10:02-10:15 UTC; on-call notified via manual calls and fallback provider. Investigating root cause." Will keep it updated.
alex: thanks. postmortem owners: jon + maya + rebecca. Action items: 1) investigate why rate-window threshold reacted so aggressively, 2) add alert in notify to surface gateway 429 spike, 3) add automatic failover to fallback with no suppressor for first 60s of spike.
maya: I'll pull telemetry and correlate with customer reports, and check if the suppressor logic uses rolling-window size correctly.
jon: I'll add a protective circuit-breaker to avoid global suppressor flips from a single provider's 429 storm.
rebecca: we manually restarted notify-router after route switch, confirmed fallback fanout healthy. monitoring dashboards show delivery success rising to normal.
alex: final check: are there any customers still affected? rebecca?
rebecca: none reported after 10:16. I'll keep the status page note until postmortem is published.
ops-bot: [automated] incident: severity=sev2 state=mitigated assigned=[jon,maya,rebecca]
alex: thanks everyone — we'll run the postmortem and schedule a config rollback/patch. :thumbsup:
